title: Kinhold Update: A look at how you can direct your villagers to dig out the voxel terrain
author: SweetKarmaz
selftext: Kinhold is being made with Claude Code. This clip shows the player selecting where in a mountain to have their villagers dig. Normally, villagers dig based on what resources are needed for the crafting queues, but you can direct them. This is a small village digging a little room out of a mountain. As they build, they will place lanterns near walls, as it can get dark underground. As it gets to be night, the villagers go to bed, and when they woke up they finished the dig. Everything dug out of the mountain (including dirt) are resources that the villagers brought to the settlements storage.

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: how does pathfinding work when the terrain is actively changing? like if villager A is digging a path that villager B was already relying on, do you replan on the fly or is there some kind of reservation system?

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Each cell is either walkable or not (means empty, enough headroom, solid underneath, etc) - any time digging is done or a building is placed, the cell updates immediately. The villagers cache routes, and an updated cell that impacts a cached route causes it to fail and the villager recaches an updated route. If it fails to plan 3 times in a row, its considered stranded and they can be ported back to the village. They fall if the ground is mined out from under them, if they end up stuck in the ground it pushes them to the nearest walkable cell, etc.

comments.author: ninjasaid13
comments.body: I really want to know how to do this.

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Honestly, Claude is the brains on the voxel portion, it was beyond me. I learned a lot auditing the scripts, though!

replies.author: ninjasaid13
replies.body: I wonder if it could be reused to make a game like runescape.

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Sure, you could use it for any kind of game - but if its not going to take advantage of the voxel terrain it wouldnt be worth it.

comments.author: thewowcollector
comments.body: How are you constructing the terrain?

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body:
Each new game is a randomly generated seed world (or you can manually input a seed to play a specific world).  
In numbers, each world is 6016m × 6016m x 512m height, in 0.25m voxels grouped into 32-voxel chunks. Each world is built in layers, with a few different noise fields, and different voxel ores around certain depts all over the world - with at least a few locations that reach up to the surface even if they would not by default. I didnt want everything hiding below ground. And guaranteed minimums and maximums.  
Then for the harvestables, the animals, the enemy settlements, etc, are all dictated with different rules.  
I am on the 17th version of the world generator, and there is probably one or two more before I would consider this a release worthy candidate.
